description: Every token a Rally theme may set. A theme file supplies values for these paths and no others.

groups.cmp.elicitation: The inset choice list within an agent question, distinct from its surrounding message surface.
groups.cmp.keycap: The chip a keyboard shortcut is printed on. It takes a fill of its own rather than the selected row's because it is a label, not a selection: this registry's own entry for `cmp.row.background-selected` licenses a theme to set it to `transparent` and mark selection with the marker alone, and a keycap that followed it there would disappear, having never been a selection. The letter beside an option in an agent question reads this today; the stylesheet's other keycaps still name their own fills and should land here when either is next touched.
groups.ref.color.neutral: The neutral ramp, ordered by contrast against the surface rather than by lightness, so a step means the same thing whichever way round a theme runs. Fills at the faint end, text at the strong end.
groups.ref.color.line: The line ramp. Borders are not faint fills: a theme that draws with space needs to flatten its lines without erasing the fills that share a contrast level with them.
groups.ref.space: The spacing unit. Every margin, padding and gap in the feed is a whole multiple of it, derived in the stylesheet, and the semantic spacing tokens are multiples of it too, so a theme that wants a looser or tighter feed moves one number.
groups.sys.backdrop: The window's backdrop: one painted layer behind every pane, so a theme's light runs unbroken beneath a translucent sidebar and the feed beside it rather than being repainted per pane and showing a seam at the join. Each token is a CSS `background-*` longhand under its own name, so a theme declares a backdrop the way a stylesheet would and the browser's own sizing, centring and tiling rules apply unchanged. `image` also accepts `{"svg": "<svg …>"}` for artwork drawn in the theme file and `{"url": "https://…"}` for one fetched over the network, and an array for layers.
groups.sys.color.surface: The named surfaces. Declared outright by each theme because their relationship inverts between light and dark — a dark theme makes a control recede by darkening it, a light theme by greying it.
groups.sys.color.state: The interaction washes, painted over whatever surface a control already sits on rather than replacing it. There is one hover wash for the whole product: a navigation row, a menu item, a header icon and a settings button are the same gesture under the pointer, and a reader who has to ask which wash a control takes is reading a decision that was never made. It is translucent in both appearances precisely so that one value can do that — an opaque fill has to know what is behind it, and `surface.raised-hover` did not on the canvas.
groups.sys.color.border: The three borders the stylesheet names directly; each resolves to a step on the line ramp.
groups.sys.color.brand: Rally's own colour. `ink` is the brand drawn as a mark or a label on an ordinary surface, which is a different question from `base`: the chartreuse is a fine fill on white and an illegible label on it.
groups.sys.color.accent: The hue for links and selection; keyboard focus has its own role.
groups.sys.color.success: Positive state. `fill` and `fill-edge` are a filled control — a switch that is on, a selected preset — which is neither the vivid hue nor the wash. `vivid` is the one saturated step, for a status indicator a few pixels across — the healthy dot beside a connection — where `base`, tuned for text and fills, read as grey.
groups.sys.color.badge: A count, a Needs input badge or an unread dot: the red design.html draws them in, with white digits, in both appearances. Apart from `danger`, which dark lightens until white over it fails contrast.
groups.sys.color.palette-ink: The two inks a palette fill can carry, absolute in both appearances. A fill does not change with the theme, so the ink over it must not either — the neutral ramp inverts and is the wrong source here. Which one a given fill takes is PALETTE_INK in @rally/contracts, not a judgement made in CSS.
groups.sys.color.project: The semantic identity palette shared by projects, work streams, and personal accents. Stored color keys remain stable; each light/dark appearance defines its own values so shades can be tuned for contrast without changing saved choices.
groups.sys.color.project-tint: The background of a mark drawn in a palette hue — a Channel's or a Breakout's glyph, a Sidekick's hexagon, a picker swatch. Pastel rather than the hue itself, all at one lightness and chroma per appearance so none stands out, and each a pair with its `project-ink`. A person's own colour does not use it: avatars and accents keep `project` at full saturation.
groups.sys.color.project-ink: The icon on its `project-tint`, and the stroke of a mark drawn without one (a Breakout's bare mark, a Space's icon). Every ink clears WCAG text contrast on its tint: at least 4.5:1 in the light appearance and 7:1 in the dark.
groups.sys.color.workstream: One colour per state a work stream can show a person in the sidebar and on the home screen. Every marker in the product draws from this group and nowhere else, so a state has one colour wherever it appears; which state wins when several are true at once is the client’s ordering, not the palette’s. Five of them are the run’s (`running`, `needs-input`, `completed`, `failed`, `stopped`) and three are the reader’s own (`unread`, `mentioned`, `unseen`), which is why they are one vocabulary: they compete for one dot.
groups.sys.color.scrim: What sits between a layer and what it covers. `solid` hides the backdrop outright; `veil` is the same colour at half strength, for a layer that means to leave the window it covers legible behind it.
groups.sys.color.focus: The colour of a focus indicator.
groups.sys.color.shimmer: The sweep across a loading skeleton.
groups.sys.color.glass: The light a glass shape catches: its sheen and the rim along its top edge. Brighter on a light surface than a dark one, where white reads as glare.
groups.sys.color.syntax: Syntax highlighting. `prism-react-renderer` takes a JavaScript object rather than a class, so these reach it as `var()` inside an inline style.
groups.sys.color.person: One per participant, chosen by a hash of their id. Six is enough that a repeat is rare in a room and few enough that each stays distinguishable.
groups.sys.elevation.shadow: Depth. A theme that lifts nothing sets these to `none`.
groups.sys.focus.ring: Whole box-shadow values for a focus ring, so a theme controls its spread as well as its colour.
groups.sys.space.stack: Between one turn and the next in the feed: the space under the action row a turn lays out beneath itself.
groups.sys.space.seam: Between a row and the row before it when a stretch of transcript this client has not loaded lies between them. Nothing else marks the seam, so the distance is what says the two rows are not adjacent.
groups.sys.space.group: Between one group of rows and the next.
groups.sys.space.block: Between a turn and an event row in the feed, in either direction: a turn and the work that follows it, or an event and the person's reply.
groups.sys.space.event: Between one event row and the next, and between a run's work and the answer it produced.
groups.sys.font.family: System sans-serif for application UI, including secondary windows and portals. Bundled Geist Mono remains available for code and technical content.
groups.sys.font.size: The sizes the interface sets, as against the document size a theme inherits.
groups.sys.font.weight: Weights. Only meaningful to the degree the resolved family supports them.
groups.sys.label: The four properties that decide whether a label is sentence case or letterspaced small capitals. They apply to the label over a turn in the feed as well as the one over a group of navigation rows.
groups.cmp.pane: The content pane. `background` is the fill drawn over the backdrop, so a theme that wants its backdrop to show through the feed sets it to `transparent` rather than to a colour that happens to match.
groups.cmp.sidebar: The navigation. `background` is a translucent tint, so `background-solid` exists for the narrow-width drawer, which sits over the content and cannot be see-through.
groups.cmp.marker: The mark at a row's leading edge. It is one element whose *shape* is a theme's decision and whose *colour* stays the row's state, so a theme can trade a dot for a line without the navigation losing what the dot was saying. It stretches between `inset-block` and the row, which is what lets one pair of values describe both a centred dot — `calc(50% - 3px)` — and a line that runs the height of the row.
groups.cmp.row: Inside a navigation row. `height-dense` is the floor under the rows whose height comes from their content; `height` is the floor for a single-line row. `background-selected` is the selected fill; a theme that marks selection with the marker alone sets it to `transparent`. A row's hover is not here: it is `sys.color.state.hover`, which every control in the product shares.
groups.cmp.group-label: The band a group's label sits in.
groups.cmp.bubble: The fill behind a person's turn. A theme with one continuous ground can set all three to nothing and let the message sit on the page as plain text.
groups.cmp.composer: The message composer's frame. A theme builds either shape out of the same five values: a card sets a background, a border and a radius; a rule sets them to nothing and gives `rule-color` a hairline instead, so the composer reads as a line the page rests on rather than as a box floating over it. `rule-color-focus` is what that line does when the field has focus, which is the only feedback left once the border is gone. `send-background` and `send-radius` are the send control's own frame, which follows the composer: a flat composer with a raised button on it reads as two different surfaces.
groups.cmp.feed: The reading column's width, and the identity line over a turn in it.
groups.cmp.markdown: Rendered markdown. Its colours were already tokens; its *measurements* were not, which is why Air's headings were smaller than the prose beneath them — `.markdown-body` scaled with `sys.font.size.prose` and the headings it contained stayed at a fixed 18/16/14.5/14. A theme that moves its prose size has to be able to move the scale above it, and the rhythm with it. The `article-*` values are the note detail's own scale: a note is read as a document rather than as a turn in a transcript, so its headings run larger than the feed's. Its margins are not tokens: they are the stylesheet's spacing steps, which follow `ref.space.unit`.
groups.cmp.tooltip: A surface that deliberately opposes the theme: light on a dark theme and dark on a light one. Name a token, never a literal — the ramp inverts with the appearance, so one alias in both appearance files gives the opposition for free, and the hue then follows the palette instead of being chosen twice by hand. The ink is `sys.color.text.on-inverse`, which every other inverted surface already reads. The fill is a ramp step rather than `sys.color.surface.inverse-hover`, whose two values it happens to match: that token is a *hover* state and a tooltip has no rest to hover from, and the system has no resting `surface.inverse` sibling to point at — which is also why the inverted controls in `app.css` take their resting fill from `sys.color.text.default`. Adding that sibling would give this and those four rules one pair to share; until it exists, prefer the ramp step over borrowing a state token for its value. `HUELESS_SURFACES` in `scripts/build-theme-assets.test.mjs` holds these two to no hue in either appearance; the partition guard beside it never could, because it compares raw JSON text.
groups.cmp.segmented: The track behind an exclusive-choice strip. Its one value is the recess the chosen pill sits in, and the pill is `sys.color.surface.raised`, so the two have to move apart in both appearances. That is why the track is not a neutral step: light recesses *down* from the card it sits on and dark recesses further down again, and the one step that reads as a recess in dark is the raised fill itself.
groups.cmp.meter: A meter: a fill on a track, for a measured share such as the week's quota left. The fill is the text colour, near-black in light and near-white in dark, not the brand: a measured share is information, and the brand yellow is kept for accents. `fill-warning` replaces it when the value is low enough to warn about. The track is not `sys.color.surface.sunken` in light because a settings card is that same grey there, so the empty part of a meter drawn on a card would vanish; dark keeps the sunken fill, which already reads as a recess on both the card and a menu.
groups.cmp.toggle: A switch. The knob is white on a grey track in a light theme, which is about two to one; the lift from `sys.elevation.shadow.sm` is what makes the off state read as a control.
groups.cmp.button: Neutral primary actions, separate from brand identity and semantic danger or success states.
groups.cmp.control: Shared secondary controls, independent of message and sidebar geometry. `background-quiet` is the resting fill of a control drawn as a faint chip rather than as a bordered box — the composer’s round tools, the send and stop buttons, the collapsed sidebar’s search pill. It carries the same weight as `sys.color.state.hover` today and is named apart from it on purpose: one is what a control looks like at rest and the other is what any control looks like under the pointer, and a change to either should not have to argue about the other.
groups.cmp.surface: Shared secondary cards, dialogs and menus, independent of message bubbles.
